recent_articles.title: Stand-off over Bengaluru Development portfolio likely to be discussed in Delhi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Krishna Byre Gowda**, Karnataka's Minister for Bengaluru Development, is reportedly dissatisfied with the truncated portfolio he received.  He has expressed his discontent to **Congress Central leadership**, amidst a critical monsoon season and an absence of elected councillors in Bengaluru due to delayed elections for five corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA).

recent_articles.title: As logjam over Bengaluru development portfolio continues, insiders point fingers at CM Shivakumar | Bangalore News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Krishna Byre Gowda**, the newly appointed **Bengaluru development minister**, has yet to assume his role five days after appointment due to confusion over the scope of his portfolio.  **D K Shivakumar**, the **Karnataka Chief Minister**, retained control over key agencies like the **Bangalore Development Authority (BDA)** and the **Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority (BMRDA)**, sparking dissent from senior leader **Ramalinga Reddy**. Despite initial disagreements, Reddy has since taken charge of the irrigation ministry.  **Gowda**, who was in Delhi on Tuesday, has not commented on the delay.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar keeping BDA, BMRDA to drive PRR and Bidadi Township raises questions - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar** has retained control of the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) and Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority (BMRDA), despite previously assigning the portfolios to **Krishna Byre Gowda**. This decision has sparked controversy as it allows **Shivakumar** to continue overseeing key projects, including the Bengaluru Business Corridor and Bidadi Township, while **Byre Gowda** is now responsible for tunnel roads overseen by **B-SMILE**.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka Congress says all is well day after Ramalinga Reddy sends resignation over WhatsApp | Bangalore News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress party leaders**, including **Randeep Surjewala** and **Chief Minister D K Shivakumar**, resolved a crisis in the Karnataka government triggered by **Ramalinga Reddy's** resignation.  Reddy, who had publicly announced his resignation over the refusal of his demand for the Bengaluru Development minister portfolio, was granted the Irrigation Ministry instead. The resolution involved discussions between **Reddy, Shivakumar, Hariprasad**, and former CM **Siddaramaiah**.

recent_articles.title: Ramalinga Reddy resigns from Ministry, says he is ‘humiliated’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ramalinga Reddy**, a senior Congress legislator from Bengaluru, resigned after being denied the **Bengaluru Development** portfolio by **Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar**.  He stated that he would not personally submit his resignation but would do so through an official channel.  Reddy, who has been influential in East and North Bengaluru, expressed disappointment over the decision and claimed a promise made by **Shivakumar** to give him the portfolio was broken. Supporters of Reddy staged protests in his constituency.  Former Law and Parliamentary Affairs Minister H.K. Patil urged leaders to address the issue justly.

recent_articles.title: Kharge files nomination papers for Rajya Sabha polls from Karnataka - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mallikarjun Kharge**, president of the **All India Congress Committee**, filed his nomination papers for the Rajya Sabha election from Karnataka, accompanied by **Rahul Gandhi**. The other two candidates are **Mansoor Ali Khan** and **Pawan Khera**.  The elections will be held on June 18th with the Congress party expected to secure three seats. Discussions regarding portfolio allocation among ministers were reportedly underway during a car ride.

recent_articles.title: First resignation in 2-day-old DKS cabinet, Ramalinga Reddy resigns over portfolio | Bangalore News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ramalinga Reddy**, **Karnataka**'s Minister, resigned after being denied the **Bengaluru Development** portfolio.  He had previously requested this position and was offered the **Water Resources** portfolio as a compromise. **D K Shivakumar**, the Chief Minister, allocated portfolios to his 13 ministers, including **Priyank Kharge** as Home Minister and **Dr G Parameshwara** as Revenue Minister.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka Cabinet portfolios row emerges after Shivakumar Government swearing-in | Bangalore News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Newly elected **Karnataka** Chief Minister D K Shivakumar is facing challenges in allocating portfolios to his cabinet.  **Ramalinga Reddy**, a newly inducted minister, reportedly resigned after not being allocated the Bengaluru Development portfolio, which he had sought. Sources suggest that attempts were made to appease **Reddy** with other ministerial positions, but ultimately, **Krishna Byre Gowda** was chosen for the role. Other ministers are also reported to have expressed dissatisfaction with their assigned portfolios.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka cabinet portfolios allocated, but disgruntlement remains - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mr. Shivakumar**, the newly sworn-in **Karnataka** Chief Minister, allocated portfolios to his cabinet on Thursday (June 5, 2026).  The most contested portfolio, Bengaluru Development, was given to **Krishna Byre Gowda**. Senior Minister **Ramalinga Reddy** received Major and Medium Irrigation. **Priyank Kharge** will be the new Home Minister, while **G. Parameshwara** has been assigned Revenue and Sports. **Eshwar Khandre** is in charge of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj, and **Byrathi Suresh** holds Transport.  The allocation of Bengaluru Development portfolio remains a contentious issue.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka cabinet portfolios allocated, but disgruntlement remains - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mr. Shivakumar**, the newly-sworn in **Karnataka** Chief Minister, allocated portfolios to his cabinet on Thursday after a day of negotiations and discontent among some ministers.  **Krishna Byre Gowda** received the coveted Bengaluru Development portfolio previously held by Mr. Shivakumar. **Ramalinga Reddy**, who had sought the portfolio, was given Major and Medium Irrigation. Other key changes included **Priyank Kharge** as Home Minister and **G. Parameshwara** as Revenue and Sports Minister. The allocation of the Bengaluru Development portfolio is likely to remain a contentious issue in the lead-up to upcoming civic polls.

recent_articles.title: Shivakumar set to take oath as Karnataka CM in lowkey ceremony | Bangalore News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D K Shivakumar**, the newly elected 34th Chief Minister of **Karnataka**, will take his oath on Wednesday alongside a first batch of around 10 ministers. The ceremony, held at the state Lok Bhavan with limited fanfare, is expected to include several senior ministers from the Siddaramaiah cabinet and two young ministers, including **Priyank Kharge** and **Krishna Byre Gowda**.  The Congress leadership has opted for a low-key swearing-in, prioritizing balancing caste equations in the new cabinet. **Rahul Gandhi**, **Mallikarjun Kharge**, and **V D Satheesan** are expected to attend the ceremony.

recent_articles.title: Will CM-designate Shivakumar continue to hold charge of Bengaluru Development portfolio? - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Will D.K. Shivakumar**, the Chief Minister, faces pushback from **Congress Ministers** in Bengaluru who advocate for a full-time minister for the city's development portfolio.  Senior ministers like **Ramalinga Reddy**, **K.J. George**, and **Krishna Byre Gowda** are mentioned as potential candidates. While Shivakumar is keen to retain the portfolio, some argue his personal involvement has been significant in driving key projects and shaping Bengaluru's governance.

recent_articles.title: Congress unveils ‘Bhu Guarantee’ in Karnataka - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the **Deputy Chief Minister** of Karnataka, unveiled the "sixth guarantee" — Bhu Guarantee — which includes a 60% discount on conversion fees for B-Khata to A-Khata properties within Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) limits. The scheme also offers a 50% reduction in regularisation costs for buildings constructed before 2008 on BDA land, and a 15% setback relaxation as per the Town Planning Act. These announcements come amidst discussions about holding civic elections in Bengaluru this year.  The government aims to encourage property conversions and regularizations, but faces challenges with low application rates due to high fees previously associated with these processes.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka minister D Sudhakar passes away - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D. Sudhakar**, the Minister for Planning and Statistics of **Karnataka**, passed away on Sunday at a private hospital in Bengaluru after battling a lung infection following a knee operation. He was 66 years old.  The government has declared a three-day mourning period and a holiday for schools, colleges, and government establishments on Monday. Prominent leaders across party lines have expressed condolences, including **Randeep Singh Surjewala**, the AICC general secretary in charge of Karnataka, and **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister of **Karnataka**.

recent_articles.title: After Bowring wall collapse, civic bodies begin removal of dangerous structures across Bengaluru - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following the collapse of the Lady Curzon and Bowring Hospital compound, **Bengaluru city corporations** have intensified efforts to remove dilapidated structures across the city.  **M. Maheshwar Rao**, chief commissioner of the **Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA)**, directed officials to identify and remove unsafe buildings and walls within GBA limits. **Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar** also instructed authorities to address hazardous trees, weak branches, and structurally unsound structures. Special teams have been formed to carry out precautionary measures, with civic bodies already beginning demolition efforts on several sites.

recent_articles.title: Davangere South bypolls: Tanveer Sait too alleges embarrassment to Congress by some minority leaders - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tanveer Sait**, former Minister and **KPCC** working president, criticized the party's handling of the recent Davangere South by-election, claiming confusion among voters was caused by internal conflicts. He stated that while minority leaders seeking a ticket for their community members is not wrong, they should follow party decisions.  Sait also defended the decision to field Samarth, grandson of **Shamanur Shivashankarappa**, citing the "sympathy" factor in ticket distribution and acknowledged past instances where he benefited from this practice. He further claimed that despite instructions from **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** and **KPCC president D.K. Shivakumar** to address rebel leaders' concerns, they failed to act.  Local leaders have called for action against those responsible for voter confusion.

recent_articles.title: Bengaluru corporations to present budgets on March 27–28 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA)** announced that city corporations will present their respective budgets on Friday and Saturday, March 27 and 28. The total budget outlay is expected to exceed ₹21,000 crore, with the **West Corporation** receiving the highest allocation due to government funding.  The State government has pledged financial assistance for corporations facing deficits. All corporations will have a separate allocation for footpaths and prioritize parks and lakes.

recent_articles.title: Govt. plans to close Government Flying Training School at Jakkur to develop club for MLAs, MPs, officials: BJP - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **R. Ashok**, leader of the Opposition, accused the **Congress** government of planning to shut down Bengaluru's GFTS at Jakkur to build an exclusive club for politicians and bureaucrats. He alleged that a senior IAS officer had proposed this plan in consultation with a developer from Rajasthan.  **K.J. George**, Energy Minister, suggested using the land for a major sports complex, while **Krishna Byre Gowda**, Revenue Minister, previously opposed the idea of an executive club.

recent_articles.title: Do not villainise subsidies as they strengthen our economy: Krishna Byre Gowda - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Revenue Minister Krishna Byre Gowda** defended the use of subsidies in Karnataka, citing its positive impact on the state's economy. He argued that providing money to low-income individuals stimulates consumer demand and boosts economic growth, particularly during recessions. **Gowda** cited Keynesian economics and emphasized the ripple effect of circulating funds through the economy.  He also criticized the "criminalization" of subsidies in various countries, including India.

recent_articles.title: 1.12 lakh acres donated to Waqf Board, but it currently controls only 20,054 acres: Zameer - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **B.Z. Zameer Ahmed Khan**, the **Karnataka Housing, Waqf and Minority Welfare Minister**, stated that over 1.12 lakh acres of land had been donated to the **Waqf Board** but currently they control only 20,054 acres.  Khan also revealed that 17,969 acres were encroached upon by members of the Muslim community. The **Leader of the Opposition R.
